title: Tags and environments (dev, staging, production)
hook: Tags are key-value metadata on AWS resources. They power cost allocation, automation, and access conditions — but they are not a security boundary. Use separate accounts for prod isolation; use tags for attribution and policy scoping within an account.

blocks.text: Every taggable AWS resource can carry tags like Environment=production, Team=platform, Application=orders-api. AWS Tag Editor and Resource Groups search across services. Cost allocation tags must be activated in the billing console before Cost Explorer groups by them. Tag policies in Organizations enforce required keys. Environment separation (dev, staging, prod) is best done with separate accounts; tags distinguish resources within an account and drive IaC parameterization.

entries.plainDefinition: A tag activated for billing reports so spend can be grouped by that key.
entries.example: Environment tag appears in Cost Explorer after activation.

entries.plainDefinition: Org rule requiring specific tag keys/values on resources.
entries.example: Require Environment with allowed values dev, staging, prod.

entries.plainDefinition: Query engine to find resources matching tag filters across services.

blocks.text: Untagged resources are invisible to finance and dangerous in incident response ('which team owns this NAT Gateway?'). SCPs and IAM conditions can use aws:RequestTag and aws:ResourceTag for guardrails — e.g., deny ec2:RunInstances unless Environment tag is present. Tags complement, not replace, account-level isolation.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Tags for cost and automation; accounts for security boundaries. Require tags at deploy time via IaC and tag policies.

snippet.label: CLI: tag resources and find untagged EC2
snippet.code:
aws ec2 create-tags \
  --resources i-0abc123 \
  --tags Key=Environment,Value=prod Key=Application,Value=orders-api

aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources \
  --resource-type-filters ec2:instance \
  --tag-filters Key=Environment,Values=prod
snippet.explanation: create-tags at launch time. Resource Groups API inventories by tag across the account.

snippet.label: CloudFormation: mandatory tags on all resources
snippet.code:
Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    AllowedValues: [dev, staging, prod]
Resources:
  AppInstance:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Instance
    Properties:
      InstanceType: t3.micro
      ImageId: ami-0c55b159cbfafe1f0
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: Application
          Value: orders-api
snippet.explanation: Parameterize Environment; every stack resource inherits consistent tags from IaC.

snippet.label: CloudFormation: SCP require Environment tag on create
snippet.code:
Statement:
  - Effect: Deny
    Action:
      - ec2:RunInstances
      - rds:CreateDBInstance
    Resource: '*'
    Condition:
      Null:
        aws:RequestTag/Environment: 'true'
snippet.explanation: Org SCP denies resource creation without Environment tag — governance at API level.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Tagging manually after creation — resources miss billing window. Using Environment=prod tag as sole security control. Not activating cost allocation tags so finance cannot see team spend.

interviewTakeaways: Tags are metadata for cost, automation, and IAM conditions — not security isolation.
Separate accounts for prod; tags for attribution and policy scoping within accounts.
Activate cost allocation tags; enforce required keys via tag policies and SCP conditions.
60s: Tags = cost and ops. Accounts = security boundary. Standard keys: Environment, Team, Application. Enforce at create via IaC and SCP aws:RequestTag conditions.
Follow-up: how do tag policies differ from SCP tag conditions?
commonPitfalls: Treating Environment=prod tag as equivalent to a prod account — gets you rejected in security-focused interviews.
Strong answer: accounts isolate blast radius; tags allocate cost and drive automation within account.
Forgetting to activate cost allocation tags — tags exist but Cost Explorer ignores them.
Retroactive tagging after month-end close — spend already unattributed.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Apply Tags.of(scope).add('Environment', props.env) in CDK Aspects so every construct gets tags at synth — same discipline as eslint rules for code quality.
